title: Performance Max for a Local Business: Worth It? 7 Checks

facts.fact: Store Growers says a PMax campaign needs roughly 20 to 30 conversions a month per campaign (vendor citing a third party).
facts.quote: One says roughly 20 to 30 conversions a month per campaign (Store Growers)

facts.fact: Digital Marketing Knight suggests 15 to 50 conversions a month as a rule of thumb for PMax (vendor citing a third party).
facts.quote: another suggests 15 to 50 a month as a rule of thumb (Digital Marketing Knight)

facts.fact: Black Propeller says 50 or more conversions helps PMax campaigns exit the learning phase faster (vendor citing a third party).
facts.quote: another says 50 or more helps campaigns exit learning faster (Black Propeller).

facts.fact: SEOQuick estimates the PMax learning period ranges from 6 days to 6 weeks (third-party estimate cited by the vendor).
facts.quote: estimates range from 6 days to 6 weeks (SEOQuick)

facts.fact: George Tsiros estimates the PMax learning period at 4 to 6 weeks (third-party estimate cited by the vendor).
Digital Marketing Knight suggests a PMax budget of about 10 times the target cost per conversion per day (third-party guidance cited by the vendor).
facts.unit: times target cost per conversion per day
facts.quote: one guide suggests about 10 times your target cost per conversion per day (Digital Marketing Knight)

facts.fact: Store Growers says to avoid PMax under roughly $1,000 a month in the e-commerce context (third-party claim cited by the vendor).
facts.quote: Another says to avoid PMax under roughly $1,000 a month in the e-commerce context (Store Growers).

facts.fact: George Tsiros reports that most accounts with poor PMax results made structural changes in weeks two to three, which reset learning (third-party observation cited by the vendor).
facts.quote: Most accounts reporting poor results made structural changes in weeks two to three, which reset learning (George Tsiros).

facts.fact: Google lets advertisers write up to 15 headlines of 30 characters for a PMax campaign.
facts.quote: Google lets you write up to 15 headlines of 30 characters.

facts.fact: Google recommends store goals only for accounts eligible for store visits (per AdNabu).
facts.quote: Google recommends store goals only for accounts eligible for store visits (AdNabu).

facts.fact: The vendor's own checklist says a business should be able to fund 4 to 6 weeks of PMax without cutting budget.
facts.quote: Budget:** you can fund 4 to 6 weeks without cutting it.

facts.fact: The vendor's own checklist says a business should be able to reach about 20 to 30 conversions a month before starting PMax.
facts.quote: Volume:** you can reach about 20 to 30 conversions a month.

facts.fact: The vendor advises skipping PMax if there are fewer than about 15 reliable conversions a month.
facts.quote: You have fewer than about 15 reliable conversions a month.

facts.fact: The vendor states its reading that a budget unable to buy about 20 to 30 real leads a month means PMax will struggle to learn is its own inference, not a Google rule.
facts.quote: Our reading, which is an inference and not a Google rule: if your budget can’t buy about 20 to 30 real leads a month, PMax will struggle to learn.

facts.fact: Google's channel performance report includes offline conversions such as local actions, store visits and store sales, according to Google Ads Help as cited by the vendor.
facts.quote: Google’s channel performance report includes offline conversions such as local actions, store visits and store sales (Google Ads Help).

facts.fact: PMax serves ads across Google's Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and Maps channels from one campaign.
facts.quote: serves ads across Google’s channels, including Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and Maps, from one campaign.
